messages:
alex: Kicking off handoff. Noticed a sustained uptick in regen-rate for long-context models in us-east-2 since ~00:40 UTC. Root cause looks like kvproxy connection pool exhaustion -> increased cache miss and token churn. 502/503s from downstream inference nodes.
maya: Saw the alerts. Any link to the midnight kvproxy deploy? I saw two OOM restarts on the perf cluster.
noah: Correlating now. The logs show many `pool_queue_timeout` events on kvproxy and a growing number of TCP TIME_WAIT sockets. Not classic OOM; more like file-descriptor / connection saturation under heavy prefix cache miss pattern.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-17T00:35:02 UTC — kvproxy/2026.3.17 applied to canary (3/20). Monitoring.
alex: Mitigations applied while oncall: 1) Routed 20% of traffic for model-family `companion-3b` to `quantized-medium-fallback` 2) Increased kvproxy max_connections & reduced keepalive on problematic nodes 3) Shortened prefix-KV prefetch window to avoid bursty cache reads.
ops-support: FYI — a couple of enterprise tenants in us-east-2 reported higher latencies; CS ticket numbers: CS-8123, CS-8124.
sri: Added a rate-limit on aggressive prefetches to avoid spiking Redis with large multi-get. Also muted duplicate regen alerts for same tenant to reduce noise.
maya: Does the fallback affect quality? Any metrics on hallucination/regression?
noah: Fallback reduces memory pressure but has a small eval delta (BLEU-style drop ~0.5 on our regen-checkset). Tradeoff seems acceptable for availability. We'll track quality metrics on the rollout.
alex: Commands for next person:

```bash
# inspect kvproxy pool
dd_query "kvproxy.pool_queue{env:prod,region:us-east-2}.rollup(max, 1m)"
# flip fallback weight
rhctl route set model-family/companion-3b --weight quantized-medium-fallback=20
# revert kvproxy image if needed
kubectl -n infra set image deploy/kvproxy kvproxy=kvproxy/2026.3.15
```
noah: Datadog queries to watch:
- `sum:redwood.inference.regen_count{env:prod,region:us-east-2} by {tenant}`
- `avg:last_value(kvproxy.pool_queue){env:prod,region:us-east-2}`
- `count:redis.command.timeouts{env:prod,region:us-east-2}`
alex: Handoff checklist for incoming oncall:
- Keep fallback routing at 20% for 90 minutes while observing pool_queue and redis timeouts
- If `kvproxy.pool_queue` > 75% for 5m, escalate to infra and roll back kvproxy to 2026.3.15
- If redis timeouts persist after kvproxy rollback, open infra bridge and include redis-ops

maya: I'm offline shortly but on pager if needed. Will check the CS queue after handoff.
sri: I'll follow up in the morning with a small postmortem: timeline, root-cause hypotheses (conn saturation vs fd leak), and proposed mitigation (circuit-breaker on prefetch + fd tuning).
alex: Created incident INC-2026-0512 with initial notes + mitigations. Adding logs and timelines next. Handoff complete. :thumbsup:
